pd-autopage: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: SEV2 - metrics-pipeline.prom-scrape-failure fired for prom-scrape-job-prod (alert rule: prom_scrape_failures)
incident-bot: Alert details: prom-scrape-job-prod failing to scrape multiple targets in eu-west-1 for ~6m. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prometheus-scrape-failures. Suggested first steps: check exporter pods, network, and scrape targets. Affected services: metrics-ingest-consumer, prom-exporters, kafka-ingest.
amanda (sre-oncall): Acked. I'm on it. @bob can you check infra/networking side while I look at Prometheus and exporters?
bob (platform): On it. Quickly checking node / network metrics. Initial look: no obvious node network flaps, but I see increased connection resets from exporter hosts to prom-server around 11:03 UTC.
carla (eng-ml): FYI noticed alerts about missing customer metrics on dashboards, some teams pinging support.
amanda (sre-oncall): Ok. Amanda running quick check on scrapes: kubectl logs on prom-exporter shows `dial tcp x.x.x.x:9100: connect: connection refused` for several targets. Also seeing scrape latency spike. Will try a rolling restart of exporters in eu-west-1.
amanda (sre-oncall): Commands I'm going to run (will run one-at-time):
```
kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l app=prom-exporter -o wide
kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deployment/prom-exporters-eu-west1
```
amanda (sre-oncall): Rolling restart started. Doing one node at a time per runbook. Please hold alerts for a few mins while we stabilize. I'll update here.
bob (platform): While Amanda restarts, I'm checking Kafka ingestion backlog. consumer-group `metrics-ingest` lag is high for topic `logs-raw`.
```
kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka-1:9092 --group metrics-ingest --describe
TOPIC          PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG
logs-raw       0          125000          130500          5500
```
bob (platform): Looks like log ingestion lag is contributing to missing logs -> missing derived metrics. Scaling ingest consumer to bring down lag.
bob (platform): Scaling metrics-ingest deployment to 6 replicas for burst
```
kubectl -n ingest scale deployment/metrics-ingest --replicas=6
```
carla (eng-ml): Noted. I'll start a quick sanity check on downstream aggregator after Amanda confirms exporters are healthy.
amanda (sre-oncall): First wave of exporter pods restarted, scrapes returning for ~60% targets. Some targets still failing due to `connection refused` on specific host 10.12.5.22. Investigating host-level issue.
dan (support): Seeing ~12 customer reports about alerts missing; tickets being triaged. No critical customer outages reported yet but dashboards missing important SLO graphs.
amanda (sre-oncall): Found that a recent host OS patch on 10.12.5.22 restarted node-local exporter and left firewall rules incomplete (iptables rule ordering). I'm going to cordon & drain that node and remove the bad iptables rule, then uncordon.
amanda (sre-oncall): Commands executed:
```
kubectl cordon node/10.12.5.22
kubectl drain node/10.12.5.22 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
ssh ops@10.12.5.22 sudo iptables -D INPUT 5  # remove blocking rule
kubectl uncordon node/10.12.5.22
```
amanda (sre-oncall): Node fix applied. Exporter on that host now reachable, scrapes recovered for that host.
bob (platform): Kafka consumer replicas scaled, lag dropping. Current lag per partition ~200-600 each, trending down.
```
kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka-1:9092 --group metrics-ingest --describe
TOPIC          PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG
logs-raw       0          130200          130500          300
```
amanda (sre-oncall): Good. I'm going to temporarily suppress noisy prom_scrape_failures alerts for eu-west-1 for 30m while we finish verification (muting via alertmanager).
incident-bot: Alertmanager: Silenced rule `prom_scrape_failures` for label region=eu-west-1 for 30m by amanda (sre-oncall).
amanda (sre-oncall): Handing off to @carla for post-recovery validation and follow-up. I've left notes in PD and the runbook. Current state: scrapes recovered, log ingestion lag decreasing, customers seeing metrics return. I'll create a follow-up ticket for root cause and postmortem.
carla (eng-ml): Taking handoff. I'll run end-to-end checks on derived metrics and confirm with product teams. Also will coordinate postmortem.
dan (support): Thanks @amanda. I updated customer tickets: 12 reports consolidated into one incident (INC-4321), customers notified with status update: ETA ~30-45m to full parity. Will keep them informed.
amanda (sre-oncall): Summary: cause = host-level firewall rule after OS patch; impact = temporary missing metrics and dashboards for some customers + increased log ingestion lag; mitigation = restarted exporters, drained/fixed node, scaled ingestion consumers, silenced noisy alerts. Next steps = postmortem ticket, follow-up on patch automation to prevent iptables ordering regression.
carla (eng-ml): I'll open the postmortem and tag infra, releases, and support. Assigning to amanda + bob for RCA. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
pd-autopage: PagerDuty: Alert acknowledged and resolved (status: recovered).
